title: Revenue Recognition, Billing, Budgeting & Procurement Guidance (2026)
author: Elena Ramirez
body:
Purpose
This page defines Redwood Inference’s consolidated guidance for budgeting & forecasting, contracts & legal approval processes, procurement procedures, and revenue recognition & billing policies. The intent is to ensure consistent, auditable financial practice across teams and to align operational procedures with ASC 606 principles used by our accounting team.

Scope
Applies to: all Redwood employees and contractors who request budget/POs, negotiate or sign contracts, engage vendors, deliver billable services, or record revenue.
Exceptions: specialized enterprise or regulatory engagements requiring legal/finance exceptions must follow the Exceptions process below.

Definitions
- Subscription revenue: recurring fees for access to Redwood hosted services (hosted API, console).
- Dedicated/Private contracts: reserved capacity or private deployment engagements with upfront commitments.
- Usage-based revenue: metered charges (per-token, per-embedding unit).
- Professional services: one-time implementation, migration, or integration services.
- Deferred revenue: cash received but not yet recognized as revenue under ASC 606.

Owners & Roles
- Finance (Revenue Accounting): final authority for revenue recognition treatment and GL mapping.
- Legal: contract review and clause approval.
- Procurement: vendor onboarding and PO issuance.
- Product/Eng/Customer Success: commercial negotiations, SOW definitions, and delivery verification.
- Requestor: initiates purchase or contract request and maintains delivery evidence.

Section 1 — Budgeting and Forecasting (cadence & responsibilities)
1) Cadence and inputs:
   - Annual operating plan (AOP): prepared by Finance with inputs from Product, Eng, SRE, Sales and GTM teams. Target completion: October for next fiscal year.
   - Quarterly re-forecast: rolling 12-month view updated within 15 business days after quarter close.
   - Monthly actuals vs. forecast review: variance analysis required for any variance > 10% of line item.
2) Key inputs:
   - Sales bookings and committed pipeline (from CRM)
   - Usage trends (token throughput, embedding calls) from Observability and Billing exports
   - Headcount & hiring plan (HR input)
   - Capital and reserved capacity commitments (Infra / Eng input)
3) Deliverables and approvals:
   - Budget submission: Cost center owners submit proposed budgets to Finance via the Budgeting template (XLSX link referenced in related_pages).
   - Finance consolidates and presents to Finance Leadership for approval. Final AOP approved by CFO and CEO.
   - Material changes (> $250k annual impact) require Finance Leadership sign-off and RM approval.

Section 2 — Contracts & Legal Process
1) Contract types and required review level:
   - Standard SaaS Order Form (<= $250k ARR): Legal self-serve template; Sales may execute after Legal tech review.
   - Enterprise Agreement / Private Deployments / Dedicated (> $250k ARR or custom SLAs): Legal + Finance + Security review required.
   - Professional Services SOWs: Finance must review fees and revenue treatment; Legal reviews IP and liability clauses.
2) Required contractual clauses (minimum):
   - Scope of services, deliverables, and acceptance criteria
   - Pricing, billing cadence, taxes and payment terms (Net 30 default)
   - Data residency and confidentiality (customer-specific for Private deployments)
   - Limitation of liability and indemnity (legal-approved caps)
   - Termination and refund/credit mechanics
   - Audit rights where required by enterprise customers
3) Approval workflow (high level):
   - Sales creates draft using Contract Template Manager -> Legal review -> Finance & Security review (if applicable) -> Executive approval for non-standard commercial terms -> Counterparty signature -> Execute and upload to CLM (Contract Lifecycle Management).
4) Sign-off thresholds (approval matrix):
   | Approval Type | Threshold |
   |---------------|-----------|
   | Sales-only execution | <= $250k ARR; standard terms |
   | Legal + Finance | > $250k and <= $1M or custom SLA/termination clauses |
   | Executive (CFO/CEO) | > $1M, atypical indemnities, or >90 days payment terms |

Section 3 — Procurement Procedures
1) Purchase request and PO issuance:
   - All purchases of goods and services must be requested through the Procurement portal (link in related_pages) and include a completed Purchase Request Form: justification, GL code, cost center, vendor, and SOW or quote.
   - Procurement generates a PO for approved requests before vendor work begins. Work started without PO may be denied payment unless retroactively approved by Procurement + Finance.
2) Vendor onboarding requirements:
   - Vendor risk assessment (procurement owns running vendor through security questionnaire)
   - Signed contract or PO; W9/Tax forms and bank/ACH details on file
   - Insurance certificates for vendors providing on-site or high-risk services
3) Approval matrix (examples):
   | Role | Approval Limit |
   |------|----------------|
   | Cost center manager | <= $25k |
   | Department head | <= $100k |
   | Procurement Director | <= $250k |
   | CFO | > $250k |
4) Exceptions and emergency purchases:
   - Emergency purchases must be documented in an Emergency Purchase Form with post-facto approvals from Procurement Director and Finance within 5 business days.

Section 4 — Revenue Recognition and Billing Policies
Principles: align with ASC 606 — identify performance obligations, determine transaction price, allocate price to performance obligations, recognize revenue when performance obligations are satisfied.
1) Recognition rules by revenue type:
   - Subscription (monthly/annual): Recognize ratably over the service period once the customer has access and the service is available. For upfront annual prepayments, record cash to Deferred Revenue and recognize monthly.
   - Dedicated / Reserved capacity: If customer prepays for committed capacity with guaranteed availability, recognize revenue over the committed term. Any implementation or onboarding services billed separately are recognized when the service is delivered/accepted.
   - Usage-based billing: Recognize when usage occurs. Monthly metered usage is invoiced in the subsequent billing cycle and recognized in the period the usage occurred.
   - Professional services: Recognize upon delivery and customer acceptance per SOW or based on % completion method if contractually specified and reliably measurable.
2) Billing cadence and invoicing rules:
   - Default payment terms: Net 30 from invoice date. Exceptions require Executive approval.
   - Invoicing schedule: Monthly for usage and subscription (unless annual prepay); milestone invoicing allowed for professional services with defined acceptance milestones in SOW.
   - Proration: New or cancelled subscriptions mid-period are prorated to the day using a 365-day year.
   - Credits and refunds: Customer credit memo created for approved refunds; refunds route through Finance and require a customer credit request and CS validation.
3) Deferred revenue and cutoffs:
   - Cutoff: Revenue recognized in the period services were performed. Finance performs monthly deferred revenue roll-forward and reconciliations.
   - Material adjustments (> $50k) to deferred revenue require Finance Director approval and must be documented with rationale and supporting ledgers.
4) Revenue accounting entries (examples):
   - Annual prepaid subscription collected (cash receipt):
     Dr Cash 100,000
     Cr Deferred Revenue 100,000
     (Monthly recognition for 12 months: Dr Deferred Revenue 8,333.33; Cr Revenue 8,333.33)
   - Usage invoice recognized in same month of usage when invoiced subsequent month:
     Dr Accounts Receivable 12,000
     Cr Revenue 12,000

Section 5 — Contracts, Billing & Accounting Operational Checklist
- Contract executed and uploaded to CLM before first invoice.
- Commercial terms (billing cadence, payment terms, taxes) captured in CRM and synced to Billing system.
- GL code and cost center validated before PO issuance.
- Evidence of delivery/acceptance for professional services retained in SOW folder.
- Customer invoices issued and sent to correct AP contact; failed invoices flagged to CS and Finance within 2 business days.

Section 6 — Auditability, Reporting & Controls
- Monthly close tasks include deferred revenue reconciliation, AR aging analysis, and revenue variance review.
- Segregation of duties: Sales/RevOps cannot post revenue journal entries; Finance posts close journals.
- Access control: Billing system access granted by Finance with 2FA and role-based permissions.
- Quarterly internal review: Procurement and Contracts to provide exception reports to Audit.

Section 7 — Exceptions & Escalation
- Exceptions to standard templates or thresholds require written justification, Legal & Finance approval, and a signed Executive waiver if above sign-off thresholds.
- Dispute handling: CS owns initial customer disputes; material billing disputes (> $25k) escalate to Head of Customer Success and Finance for joint resolution.

Appendix A — Quick Reference Tables
Approval matrix (summary):
| Item | <= $25k | $25k-$100k | $100k-$250k | > $250k |
|------|--------:|-----------:|------------:|-------:|
| Purchases | Cost center mgr | Dept head | Procurement Dir | CFO |
| Contract execution | Sales-only | Legal review | Legal+Finance | Executive sign-off |

Appendix B — Common Journal Templates
- Receive cash for annual prepay:
  Dr Cash
  Cr Deferred Revenue
- Monthly recognition for subscriptions:
  Dr Deferred Revenue
  Cr Subscription Revenue
- Recognize professional services after acceptance:
  Dr Accounts Receivable
  Cr Professional Services Revenue
